disclaimer: No player analytics are available for any of the three games (SRC-901). Every retention statement here is a RETENTION_HYPOTHESIS unless explicitly marked otherwise. Nothing in this file proves a feature increases retention.

short_term_pull.hypothesis: First hatch + Index entry gives an early collection win

mid_long_term_pull.hypothesis: Biome depth + full Index create long targets

return_triggers.hypothesis: Group join / like rewards (per official description)

monotony_risk.hypothesis: Single verb loop (swing → carry → deposit) may feel repetitive without event content; no events observed

frustration_risk.hypothesis: Losing a finished run to a guard or a rival stealer at the last moment

short_term_pull.hypothesis: Early hatches + treadmill upgrade give visible speed gains

mid_long_term_pull.hypothesis: Three parallel collection axes (rarity, size, mutation) extend the chase

monotony_risk.hypothesis: If theft is the only interaction verb, sessions may depend heavily on other players being present

frustration_risk.hypothesis: Being robbed repeatedly by stronger players

short_term_pull.hypothesis: Find egg → hatch → immediately ride creates a fast first-payoff loop

mid_long_term_pull.hypothesis: Rarity ladder up to 1-in-50M plus mutations plus possible rebirth multipliers

return_triggers.hypothesis: Seasonal event (page title carried [🎃EVENT]) may drive return visits

monotony_risk.hypothesis: Exploration-only loop with no observed combat/PvP/social verbs

frustration_risk.hypothesis: Missing a timed egg or losing a race for spawn to another player

cross_game_note: Break and Steal an Egg and Steal An Egg both create tension through theft risk; Ride A Pet appears to create tension through time/spawn competition instead. This asymmetry is the most promising comparative angle for update design — but it rests on partial third-party data and must be confirmed by observation before use.
